newsitem.title: UK: MFI says current trade meets expectations.
newsitem.headline: MFI says current trade meets expectations.

text.p: Britain's MFI Furniture Group Plc on Monday said trading since the end of its first half had been in line with expectations.
Britain's largest furniture retailer and manufacturer reported a 63 percent rise in first half pretax profits to 32.7 million pounds ($54.11 million) from 20.1 million.
Chairman Derek Hunt said in a statement, "Trading since the end of the period has been in line with our expectations."
MFI says current trade meets expectations =2
Sales in the 28 weeks to November 9 were up 15.7 percent to 440.5 million pounds from 380.6 million. Sales in Britain were up 13.5 percent, excluding new space.

Lower raw material prices and the purchasing power of a stronger pound helped boost the group's gross margin to 53.3 percent from 51.2 percent during the first half. The group operates only a small percentage of its business overseas.
The company has converted 78 of its 184 UK stores to the new style MFI Homeworks. "We are convinced our MFI Homeworks strategy is working as these stores are trading well," the chairman said.

In France, where MFI has 98 stores, sales were up 36 percent to 32.5 million pounds, representing 7.4 percent of total turnover. But MFI said difficult trading conditions in recent weeks had made it cautious about the immediate prospects for the business. ($1=.6043 Pound)
